title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk

epigraph.quote: Management credibility is measured not by the ambition of its capacity announcements, but by whether unit profitability rises as the new tonnage comes online.
epigraph.author: Capital Allocation Principle

web_blocks.html: Tracking RPEL's real progress means watching five physical and financial KPIs rather than headline revenue alone [1][21][22]. Those five metrics are (1) installed group capacity (MTPA), (2) export volume and mix, (3) EBITDA per metric tonne, (4) Debtor Days, and (5) Inventory Days and Cash Conversion Cycle [1][21][22]. Over the past five years, Chairman Sanjay Kabra and Managing Director Rajesh Kabra executed well on capacity, exports, and unit margins [1][6]. Working capital remains the main operational watchpoint [1][6].

web_blocks.takeaway: Unit profitability (EBITDA/MT) and collections (Debtor Days) have improved sharply, while Inventory Days (272) is the single operational KPI requiring close monitoring.

web_blocks.html: A CEO Walk-the-Talk Audit shows that Sanjay Kabra and Rajesh Kabra kept their promises without diluting shareholders or taking on heavy debt [1][6]. In August 2021, RPEL raised ~₹30.9 Cr via CCDs to fund its automated RPSPL Newai plant [7][17]. Skeptics doubted a small-cap mineral processor could absorb ₹60+ Cr of capex without hurting ROCE [7][17]. By FY26, that plant was running smoothly [1]. Consolidated revenue nearly doubled from ₹133 Cr in FY24 to ₹257 Cr in FY26 (₹315 Cr TTM), and ROCE rebounded from 23% to 30.3% [1].

Management's push into waste-to-value Tundish Boards and boric-acid-free RM 9901 Premix Boron lifted operating margins from 23% (FY20–FY21) to 29%–30% (FY26–TTM) [1][25][26]. Promoter shareholding held steady at 62.89% as of September 2026, virtually unchanged from 62.92% in December 2023 [1]. That stable stake keeps promoter incentives aligned with minority owners [1]. Meanwhile, total shareholders grew from 8,724 in June 2024 to 18,007 in September 2026, and FII ownership edged up from 0.00% to 0.55% [1].

web_blocks.title: Bear / Skeptic Watchpoints on Structural Execution
paragraphs: 1. Odisha JV Execution Risk: Building a 350,000 MTPA plant in Odisha (~₹100 Cr initial outlay, 80% RPEL equity) adds permitting, mine-ramp, and trial risks outside Rajasthan [6].
2. Inventory & Other Assets Creep: Inventory Days hit 272 days in FY26 [1]. Balance Sheet 'Other Assets' also climbed from ₹141 Cr (Mar 2026) to ₹193 Cr (Sep 2026), while CWIP rose to ₹15 Cr [1].
3. Institutional Concentration: Despite strong metrics, DII ownership sits at 0.04% and FII ownership at 0.55% (Sep 2026), so governance and disclosures must keep maturing [1].

book_paragraphs: If you want to know whether a management team is truly building a compounding machine or merely riding a favorable cycle, you and I should ignore the glossy adjectives in annual report letters and audit five hard operational dials. At Raghav Productivity Enhancers, those five dials are installed tonnage, export mix, EBITDA per metric tonne, debtor days, and inventory days.

Start with the capacity and mix dials. Over the past five years, Sanjay Kabra and Rajesh Kabra scaled RPEL's automated base to 414,000 metric tonnes per annum, launched brownfield expansions toward 534,000 tonnes, and in September 2026 signed an 80:20 joint venture with TRL Krosaki for another 350,000 tonnes in Odisha—putting their long-term one-million-tonne vision within striking distance. At the same time, exports grew to 30% of volume in FY25 and nearly 49% of standalone turnover in FY26 across almost forty countries. Even better, EBITDA per tonne more than doubled from roughly ₹1,245 in FY17 to around ₹2,650 by Q1 FY27.

book_subsections.title: Auditing the Kabra Brothers: Promises vs. Delivered Numbers
paragraphs: When RPEL raised ₹30.9 crore via convertible debentures in 2021 to build its automated Newai subsidiary, the obvious bear question was whether a small mineral company could digest that much fixed capital without drowning in depreciation. The answer arrived in FY26: ROCE rebounded from 23% in FY24 right back to 30.3%, and operating margins held at 29% to 30%. Meanwhile, promoter ownership stayed virtually untouched at 62.89% as of September 2026.

Now look at the collection dial: debtor days. A skeptic might assume that doubling revenue from ₹133 crore in FY24 to ₹257 crore in FY26 required loosening credit terms to small steel mills. In fact, the opposite happened. Debtor days tightened from 131 days in FY22 and 109 days in FY24 down to 83 days in FY26. That tells you customers want the product enough to pay on time.

book_subsections.title: The Amber Light: Inventory Days and Odisha Execution
paragraphs: Where does the audit flash an amber light? On the inventory dial. Inventory days climbed from 159 days in FY23 to 272 days in FY26, and in the September 2026 half-year balance sheet, Other Assets stepped up from ₹141 crore to ₹193 crore while CWIP rose to ₹15 crore. Some of that reflects prudent stocking of high-grade quartz lumps and export goods in transit, plus early spending on new capacity. Still, you and I should keep a sharp eye on whether inventory days begin trending back below 220 days once the current expansion wave settles, and whether the Odisha joint venture commissions on schedule.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Promoters holding 62.89% of equity while lifting ROCE back to 30.3% after a major capex cycle earns the benefit of the doubt—but 272 inventory days is the metric that separates a good compounder from a great one.
